transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says Russia will supply about 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. in
an effort to lower rising diesel prices.
NPR's Emily Fang reports Trump says he and Russian leader Vladimir Putin talked out the
agreement today.
It's unclear if importing Russian diesel flies in the face of a new law Trump just signed
into effect.
Named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the law put 500 percent tariffs on
Russian imports and personally sanctioned Putin.
The U.S. Treasury Department has, however, just temporarily paused its sanctions on Russian
diesel.
Trump has also temporarily paused a federal tax on diesel, though some state taxes may
still remain, all in an effort to rein in diesel prices that have shot up as much as
70 percent since the war with Iran.
His measures will likely not bring diesel prices down, however.
For example, the diesel Russia will provide amounts to just a few days of American national
diesel consumption.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
Secretary of Homeland Security Mark Wayne Mullen says ICE officers did not know a five-year-old
boy was in the car when they surrounded and shot a Dominican man in New York City last
night.
NPR's Nate Perez reports officers fired as many as seven rounds.
ICE shot Oscar Belgol in the neck when he was pulling into a parking space.
Mullen says ICE wasn't aware a child was in the car.
But he says that Belgol accelerated his speed and ramped two vehicles.
Mullen also alleges Belgol appeared to target officers with his car.
The public outcry should be also towards this criminal, this thug, this gangbanger, this
possible murderer.
Belgol was treated at a hospital but has been moved to a detention center outside New York.
New York Mayor Zoron Mamdani and Governor Kathy Hochul denounced ICE and demanded they
pause their operations.
But Mullen has vowed to continue.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
Forecasters say Hurricane Isaias will make landfall on the northern Gulf Coast tonight
as NPR's Bill Chappell reports the storm's already being felt on land lashing the coast
with tropical storm force winds.
Hurricane Isaias is currently predicted to make landfall close to the Alabama-Florida
border.
This is a major storm.
Forecasters say Isaias will stay at or near Category 3 when it arrives.
They also warned that its storm surge could reach from 6 to 9 feet along the coast.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is urging people to evacuate if they're in a high-risk zone.
We always say you hide from the wind but you run from the water.
Heavy rains will likely cause flash flooding.
Making matters worse, the rain will fall on ground that's already saturated.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Panama today, collapsing buildings and prompting
evacuations.
Aftershocks have continued, including a magnitude 6.6 quake.
The National Weather Service has issued a tsunami warning for several countries including
Panama and Colombia.
This is NPR.
Authorities in the United Arab Emirates say the fly Dubai co-pilot attacked the captain
of a flight to Tel Aviv last month, intending to crash the plane into Israel's main airport
terminal.
The UAE's top prosecutor says the Omani National aimed to cause maximum casualties, drawing
inspiration from the September 11th attacks.
The co-pilot confessed to acting alone.
Fly Dubai's checks did not indicate extremist views.
During the crisis, passengers detained him and reserve pilots landed the plane safely.
Hall of Fame tight end and Super Bowl winning coach of the Chicago Bears Mike Ditka has
died at 86, as Noah Jennings of member station WBEZ reports his look was just as legendary
as his football career.
Mike Ditka was more than a coach, he was a symbol.
His signature style, the mustache, aviator sunglasses and sweater vest inspired the recurring
Saturday Night Live sketch of the Bill Swersky superfans.
And Ditka, being the bold, outspoken person he was, appeared on the sketch once in 1993,
just days after he was fired from the Bears.
Look, this is Mike Ditka, let's get it done, sweetheart.
And you can take this to the bank, my friends, live from New York, it's Saturday night.
Ditka's likeness will live on at Bears Games, as fans continue filling the stands every
Sunday in his iconic outfit.
For NPR News, I'm Noah Jennings in Chicago.
The Draconid meteor shower peaks tonight, it comes as earth barrels through the debris
stream left by a comet.
Unlike most meteor showers, the Draconids are best viewed in the evening, just a few
hours after sunset.
This is NPR News from Washington.
